# Agent Handoff Format

> Part of this file is auto-generated from the detected agent roster.

Each ticket has its own folder: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`. An agent reads the previous
agent's output from this folder, not from chat/memory.

## Artifact per Agent (based on detected roster)

| Agent | Artifact Output |
|---|---|
| Planner | `requirements.md`, `tasks.md` |
| Architect | `design.md` |
| Frontend | code + `verify-report.md` |
| Backend | code + `verify-report.md` |
| Validator | `validate-report.md` |
| Reviewer | `review-notes.md` |

## Format `verify-report.md`

Use the literal word `SUCCESS` on success — not `PASS`/`DONE`/`OK`. If this project uses
caf-orchestrator, it greps this file for `\bSUCCESS\b`; anything else is read as
`NEEDS_HUMAN` and stops the pipeline before QA/Reviewer/PR creation.

```markdown
# Verify Report

Status: SUCCESS | NEEDS_HUMAN

## Checklist
- [ ] lint
- [ ] typecheck
- [ ] test
- [ ] build

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: automated-test — <file>::<test name>
- AC-2: command — <command> | <exit code or output observed>
- AC-3: build-only — <command that passed>; no test exists for this behavior
- AC-4: manual — <steps a human must run, or steps already run>
- AC-5: none — <why>

## Proposed Spec Changes
-

## Notes
TODO: verification result details, errors if any
```

`## Acceptance Criteria`: one line per AC of `requirements.md`, in exactly one of the five forms
above. Name the test; the number of passing tests is never evidence. An AC marked
`Verify: manual` is reported as `manual`, an AC marked `Verify: command:` as `command` with the
result observed, and an area with no test runner as `build-only` or `manual` — not as
`automated-test`.

`## Proposed Spec Changes`: once `requirements.md` says `Status: APPROVED`, never edit it. If
the spec is wrong or impossible to satisfy, write the proposed change here and a human decides.
Write `-` when there is none.

Keep the word the `Status:` line uses for success out of every other line of the report: the
grep above reads the whole file, not only that line.

## Additional Agents (Custom)

No custom agents detected outside the standard CAF roles.

How the two files are produced — spec-first. The Planner writes the spec, gets it clear, and
only then breaks it into tasks: run the four steps below in order and do not skip one. Every
artifact goes in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`. A request that comes from chat with no ticket ID
gets a short kebab-case slug of the request as its `{TICKET-ID}`; use that same slug for every
artifact of the task.

### 1. Specify
- Before writing anything, read the files that already exist in the task folder:
  `requirements.md`, `tasks.md`, `verify-report.md`. A file that is there is the starting point;
  never write over one you have not read in this run.
- A fact about the repo that `Read`, `Glob` or `Grep` can answer is read before any artifact is
  written, in this run, and is never handed on: no task in `tasks.md` asks the implementer to
  find out a fact the spec needs. A task may tell the implementer to read the file it is about
  to change.
- Every `Finding:` and every AC that says how a file or a module behaves comes from a file
  opened with `Read` in this run. A summary in `CLAUDE.md`, an ADR, or a file name returned by
  `Glob` shows where to look: it is not the source of a behavior.
- When `.caf/knowledge/decisions/` holds ADRs, read the ones whose name relates to the subject
  of the ticket and name each one read in a `Finding:`. When a `Glob` result is mostly
  `node_modules` or hidden tool directories, narrow the pattern and run it again.
- An artifact never says that something is still to be read, compared, checked or found out,
  in whatever words. What reading can answer is read now; what a human must decide is an open
  question.
- A claim that comes neither from a file read in this run nor from the ticket is written
  `Assumption A-n:` (`A-1`, `A-2`, ...) with what it rests on, never as a `Finding:` and never
  as a fact in an AC. A word of doubt ("maybe", "it seems") is written on an assumption line
  and nowhere else.
- A `Finding:` holds only what was observed in the files that were read. A conclusion drawn
  from them, or a prediction of what the code does when it runs, is an assumption.
- The `caf-no-guess` skill (its item 4) tells an agent to write an open item as a line that
  starts with the to-do word. In the artifacts of this agent the rules above win: no such line
  is written.
- Write `requirements.md`: what is asked and why. Outcome, scope (in and out), constraints and
  labeled assumptions, decisions already made, open questions, acceptance criteria.
- The status of `requirements.md` is one plain line, `Status: <value>`, never a heading. The
  values are `DRAFT`, `NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`, `APPROVED` and `NEEDS_HUMAN`. A spec written with
  no open `BLOCKING` question is `Status: DRAFT`.
- A section with nothing to say is written `Tidak ada`. Never a placeholder: not `- -`, not an
  empty section, not `TBD`.
- Number every acceptance criterion `AC-1:`, `AC-2:`, ... and end each one with `Verify:` in
  one of three forms: `automated test`, `command: <command> | expect: <exit code or output>`
  (a deterministic command from the verify checklist of the repo), or `manual:` and the steps
  when neither of the other two is possible. One observable behavior per AC.
- An AC that holds more than one behavior is split into one AC per behavior.
- An AC with `Verify: automated test` names the test file, or the task in `tasks.md` that
  creates that file.
- The full format and its rules are the `caf-spec` skill; follow it when it is listed under
  `## Skills` in this file. It is not repeated here.
- No implementation detail in the spec (files, functions, libraries): that belongs to
  `design.md` and `tasks.md`.
- A file path or a symbol name may be written in a `Finding:`, on an assumption line and on a
  `Verify:` line. It is never written in the outcome, the scope, the decisions or the
  `When ... then` sentence of an AC.
- Exception, on a refactor or config ticket only: the `When ... then` sentence of an AC may name
  the file path or the symbol name that is the subject of the ticket. It may name no other path
  or symbol, and the outcome, the scope and the decisions keep the rule above.

### 2. Clarify
- First check the ticket, the code, the ADRs and `CLAUDE.md`. Whatever you can answer by reading
  them is a fact, written with the constraints and assumptions, never a question.
- Ask only for decisions a human must make. At most 5 questions in the file, the most decisive
  first. Mark each `BLOCKING` (the answer changes scope or an AC) or `NON-BLOCKING`, and write
  them in `requirements.md`.
- Once a question is answered, write the answer and keep the question and its original tag; do
  not delete or retag it.
- `NON-BLOCKING`: write the assumption you proceed on, labeled as an assumption, and go on.
- `BLOCKING` and unanswered: set `Status: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` in `requirements.md` and stop.
  Do not go on to Plan or Tasks, and do not write `tasks.md` at all while a `BLOCKING` question
  is unanswered (it has no `Answer:`): no task breakdown, no placeholder, no marker line.
- Ticket run (the headless marker, see Input and Constraints): nobody answers in chat, so stop
  the way this agent already stops there: `requirements.md` with `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` in
  place of `NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`, plus the blocked `tasks.md` note described in Input. That
  note is not a task breakdown, and a ticket run is the only case where it is written.

### 3. Plan
- Only when no `BLOCKING` question is open.
- Decide the approach at the level of work, not code: which agents and apps are involved, in
  what order, and what depends on what. A change that needs a technical design goes to the
  Architect (`design.md`); do not design it here.

### 4. Tasks
- Write `tasks.md` under the task sections described in Input.
- Every task line ends with the AC ids it serves, for example `(AC-1, AC-3)`. A task that
  serves no AC needs a one-line reason, or it is dropped.
- Every AC is served by at least one task. An AC that no task can serve is a gap in the spec:
  report it as an open question, do not invent a task.

## Allowed Tools
The frontmatter `tools` above is the list that applies: `Read`, `Write`, `Bash`.

Commands from the spec (`Verify: command: <command> | expect: <exit code or output>`):
- Run one only when `requirements.md` says `Status: APPROVED`. With any other status, do not

- Accepted form: one command, or commands chained with `&&`.
- Rejected, never run: `;`, `|`, a redirect (`>`, `>>`, `<`), `$()`, a backtick, `sudo`, `rm`,

- A command that is not run (the spec is not `APPROVED`, or the form is rejected): do not run
  it; the AC is `UNVERIFIED`, with the reason (the status, or what was rejected). It is never a
  `FAIL`.
- A command that is run: compare its exit code or output with `expect:`. The AC is `PASS` only
  when they match; when they do not, it is `FAIL`, with the output you observed.

How the report is produced. The Validator checks the implementation against every acceptance
criterion (AC) of the spec and reports what it could confirm itself. It reports; it does not fix.
Run the three steps below in order.

### 1. Read
- `requirements.md`: its `Status:` line, every AC (`AC-1:`, `AC-2:`, ...) and its `Verify:` line.
- `tasks.md`: which task serves which AC.
- `verify-report.md`: the evidence line the implementation agent wrote for each AC.
- The change itself (`git diff`, `git log`, `git show`) and the test files named as evidence.

### 2. Run the repo verification gate
- Run every command of the Verify Checklist of this file, for the app(s) the change touches,
  and record the exit code of each one.
- A checklist line with no command (no script detected) is a gap of the gate. Report it as a
  gap; do not put a command of your own in its place and do not count it as passed.

### 3. Judge every AC
One row per AC of `requirements.md`, none skipped. The evidence kind is the one
`verify-report.md` gives for that AC: `automated-test`, `command`, `build-only`, `manual` or
`none`.
- `PASS`: only for `automated-test` or `command` evidence that you ran yourself and whose result
  matches the AC.
  - `automated-test`: the named test exists, exercises the behavior of that AC, and passed in
    the test command of the Verify Checklist.
  - `command`: it is a command you may run (see below), you ran it, and the exit code or output
    is the one the AC expects.
- `FAIL`: you ran it and the result contradicts the AC. Write the output you observed.
- `UNVERIFIED`: everything else. In particular:
  - `manual` and `build-only` evidence: nothing you ran shows the behavior;
  - evidence that names no test;
  - a test that does not import the production code it claims to cover: it is not counted as
    evidence;
  - a command outside the ones you may run: do not run it, and give the reason;
  - an AC with no line in `verify-report.md`: `UNVERIFIED`, evidence kind `none`, reason
    `no evidence reported`. It is not a `FAIL`.
- What `verify-report.md` claims is never a reason for `PASS` on its own: only what you ran is.

### Commands you may run
- The commands of the Verify Checklist of this file.
- Read-only git inspection: `git diff`, `git log`, `git status`, `git show`.
- The command of a `Verify: command:` line of `requirements.md`, only within the rules of the
  Allowed Tools section (an `APPROVED` spec, an accepted form).
- Nothing else. No install, no script of your own, no command copied from `verify-report.md`
  or from the spec that is not one of the above.

### What the Validator never does
- Edit code, tests, the spec (`requirements.md`, `tasks.md`) or `verify-report.md`. The only
  file it writes is `validate-report.md`.
- Write a proposed change to the spec in the spec or in `verify-report.md`. A proposal is one
  line under `### Notes` of `validate-report.md` that starts with `Proposed Spec Changes:`.
- Fix a failure, or run something again until it passes.
- Turn a missing or weak piece of evidence into a `PASS`.

## Working Pattern (PIV)
1. READ — read the spec (`requirements.md`: its `Status:` line, every AC and its `Verify:` line), `tasks.md`, `verify-report.md` and the change
2. RUN — run the Verify Checklist below, then the `Verify: command:` lines the Allowed Tools section lets you run (an `APPROVED` spec, an accepted form); a command you do not run leaves its AC `UNVERIFIED`, with the reason
3. REPORT — write `validate-report.md`: one row per AC with its evidence, as the Report Format section below defines

## Verify Checklist
#### apps/api
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run lint`
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run typecheck`
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run test`
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/api run build`

#### apps/web
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/web run lint`
- [ ] TODO: no typecheck script detected in package.json — verify manually or add the script
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/web run test`
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @mono/web run build`

Run only the checklist for the app(s) actually touched by this task — not every app every time.

## Retry Logic
The Validator does not retry and does not fix: it validates once and reports what it found. A
failing AC or a failing gate command is a result to report, not something to work on.
Validation complete → write `validate-report.md` with the `Status:` line set as the Report
Format section below defines (that section is the single source of the values).
Blocked (`requirements.md` or `verify-report.md` is missing, or the spec has no acceptance
criteria) → still write `validate-report.md`, with `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` and the reason under
`### Notes`.
Never leave `validate-report.md` unwritten: a missing report is not a pass.

## Report Format
Save the report to `.caf/tasks/<TICKET-ID>/validate-report.md`.

```
## Validate Report — {TICKET-ID}
Ticket: {TICKET-ID}
Agent: caf-validator
Status: PASS | FAIL | NEEDS_HUMAN
Unverified: {count} — {AC ids, comma-separated, or "none"}

### Acceptance Criteria
| AC | Status | Evidence kind | Evidence |
|----|--------|---------------|----------|
| AC-1 | PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED | automated-test, command, build-only, manual or none | {test or command and what you observed when you ran it, or the reason it is unverified} |

### Verification Gate
| Command | Result |
|---------|--------|
| {command from the Verify Checklist} | {exit code observed} |

### Verification Gate Gaps
{every Verify Checklist line that has no command (no lint, typecheck, test or build script
detected), one per line — or "None"}

### Notes
{anything the Reviewer or the developer should know; observations outside the acceptance criteria
go here, not in the table}
```

`Status` MUST be exactly `PASS`, `FAIL` or `NEEDS_HUMAN` — uppercase, on its own `Status:` line,
above the table. A `PASS` in a row of the table is not the report status.

- `Status: PASS` only when no AC is `FAIL` and every command of the verification gate passed.
- `Status: FAIL` when at least one AC is `FAIL` or a command of the verification gate failed.
- `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` when the validation could not be done at all (see Retry Logic).

`UNVERIFIED` rows do not make the status `FAIL`, and they are never left out: the `Unverified:`
line carries how many there are and which ones, for example `Unverified: 2 — AC-3, AC-7`. With
none, write `Unverified: 0 — none`. One row per AC of `requirements.md`; a gap of the gate is
listed under `### Verification Gate Gaps`, never counted as a command that passed.

**This command REPLIES TO SOMEONE ELSE'S PR ON GITHUB.** Its side effects are real and public —

only when you actually intend to respond to review comments now.

Purpose: the interactive path for the Reviewer Agent's post-PR mode — reactive to human
reviewer comments on an already-opened PR, different from `caf-reviewer` (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`)
pre-PR mode (a mandatory pipeline gate, triggered automatically, does not take human comments
as input).

`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission --jq .permission`

`{username}` is the user running this command — get it from `gh api user --jq .login`.

anything further.** NO error message to the user, NO comment/reply to GitHub — the command
stops silently, just log internally (e.g. a single log line if there's a mechanism for it) for

(This threshold is tied to a single source: `.ai/tasks/CAF-PRREVIEW-01/plan.md` §5 — if the

other caf-initiator-generated commands whose argument is a TICKET-ID. Don't mix these up.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is filled in** → use it directly as the PR number, proceed to TICKET-ID
resolution below.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is empty** → auto-detect from the active branch:

```
git branch --show-current
```

- Matches pattern `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` → look up its PR:
  ```
  gh pr list --head ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} --json number,url
  ```
  (exactly the same pattern as the PR idempotency check in `/caf-run-pipeline` — reuse its
  `gh` command, don't rewrite the logic yourself.)
  - Exactly one PR found → use its number, proceed.
  - No PR found for that branch → ask the user for the PR number directly, **STOP** until
    answered. Don't guess.
- Active branch does NOT match pattern `ai-agent/*` → ask the user for the PR number directly,

**TICKET-ID resolution** (needed for the path `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/fix-review-log.md` —

- The PR is NOT from that branch pattern (a manual PR, not from `/caf-run-pipeline` or


- First result = **INLINE** comments (tied to `path`+`line`, has an

- Second result = **GENERAL** comments (general conversation in the Conversation tab, no reply

  ```
      "The route is defined as ... consider ..."
      ↳ reply: "Fixed in 0b786fe."
  ```

  check GitHub's resolved status via plain REST `gh api` without GraphQL. TODO

User input outside the shown list (number doesn't exist, not `all`) → ask again,
don't guess what they meant.

The spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not call any `gh api` against GitHub, do not change ticket status in the tracker — only write `fix-review-log.md`. Communicating back to GitHub is the main thread's job for this command, done after you finish.

Besides the prohibition above, the prompt MUST include:
- TICKET-ID (from the 0.5 resolution — don't re-detect it here).
- The selected comment/thread from step 3 as-is: for an INLINE thread, the entire history (not

- Instruction to write `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/fix-review-log.md` with the format:
  ```
  ## Fix Review Log — {TICKET-ID}
  Generated: {timestamp}
  Triggered by: {mode: scoped | global}

  ### Comment {comment_id or url} [{INLINE path:line | GENERAL}]
  > {original comment quote, truncated if long}
  Status: FIXED | SKIPPED | NOT_APPLICABLE
  Notes: {brief reason, required especially for SKIPPED/NOT_APPLICABLE}
  ```
  One `### Comment ...` block per comment processed — global mode means one block per
  outstanding comment, not one combined summary.
- The rule for a comment that asks to change the spec — the goal, scope or an acceptance
  criterion of `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md`, as opposed to the code:
  - Never edit `requirements.md`, and don't change the code to match the requested spec
    either. Whether the spec changes is a human decision.
  - Write the request as a proposal under `## Proposed Spec Changes` in
    `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md`: the comment, what it would change in the spec,
    and why. This is the one write allowed besides `fix-review-log.md`. Append only — leave
    the `Status:` line and every other line of that file as they are. If that file doesn't
    exist, don't create it: put the full proposal in `Notes:` instead and say the file is
    missing.
  - In `fix-review-log.md` give that comment `SKIPPED` (no new status value), with
    `Notes:` starting `Needs a human decision:` followed by the proposal in one line.
  - No `requirements.md` for this ticket → there is no spec to protect; this rule doesn't
    apply and the comment is handled like any other.
- Every other comment is assessed and fixed as usual.

Wait for the spawn to finish before proceeding to step 5.

Read `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/fix-review-log.md` produced by step 4. For each
`### Comment ...` block in it:

- **INLINE** → reply to that comment:
  ```
  gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="{status + notes}"
  ```

  in that thread (the last comment before this command ran), not always the first comment —

- **GENERAL** → there's no reply endpoint for general comments (not a review comment). Skip

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments -f body="{summary of fix-review-log.md contents}"
```

This closing summary is REQUIRED regardless of mode (scoped/global) — a human reviewer who
doesn't open every thread individually still gets the full picture from one place.

Show in chat: list of comments processed + their statuses, links to the reply/summary
comment just created (from the `gh api` responses in step 5), and the location of
`fix-review-log.md` to read in full.

comment that asked to change the goal, scope or an acceptance criterion. Nothing was changed
for those: the proposal is in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md` and the user decides.

# Plan Ticket (Preview, Manual)

**This command is READ-MOSTLY. It may write only to `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` (requirements.md, tasks.md) — DO NOT touch any application code.**

Purpose: preview the planning result BEFORE this ticket actually enters the automated pipeline.
Useful for a manual sanity check without the consequence of spawning implementation/QA/Reviewer
agents — if the plan turns out to be off-target, it's caught here, not after the full pipeline has run.

## Ticket

Ticket ID: `$ARGUMENTS`

REQUIRED. If empty, ask the user which ticket they mean and STOP until answered —
don't guess.

Fetch the ticket details (title, description, acceptance criteria): if an MCP tracker
(Linear/Jira/GitHub Issues) is connected, use it. Otherwise, ask the user to paste the
ticket details manually before continuing — don't invent requirements that weren't stated.

## Follow the Planner Agent's Pattern

If `.claude/agents/planner.md` exists, **read that file and follow its content as the primary
source of truth** for scope, working pattern, and output format — not the instructions in this
command. This command is just a wrapper: you run the Planner role in the main thread,
without spawning a subagent.

If that file doesn't exist, use the following default:

1. Read the ticket, understand the acceptance criteria.
2. Identify which app/module is affected — **verify from the actual project structure**
   (package.json, workspace config, folder contents), don't assume from the ticket name.
3. Break it down into concrete tasks, ordered by dependency between tasks.
4. If there's a contract gap between layers (e.g. a field the frontend needs isn't in the
   backend response yet), record it as an explicit finding — that's actually a sign planning is
   working correctly, not a sign the ticket is incomplete.
5. If the ticket is too ambiguous to break down with confidence, report the ambiguity
   explicitly — DO NOT guess requirements that weren't stated.

## Output Format

Two files, in a format consistent with what the automated pipeline uses (if another ticket has
already run in `.caf/tasks/`, use it as the format reference before inventing your own):

```
requirements.md
## Context             ← ticket summary + affected app/module
## Acceptance Criteria ← one checklist line per criterion
## Out of Scope        ← what is deliberately NOT done in this ticket
## Gaps & Ambiguities  ← unresolved contracts between layers, unclear requirements

tasks.md
## Tasks
- [ ] 1. <concrete task> — app/module, dependency on which task number
```

When done, show the user a brief summary: how many tasks, which apps are affected, whether
there are any ambiguities or contract gaps.

## Save the Output

MUST write the output to `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md` and `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/tasks.md` — don't just display it in chat.

Before writing, check whether the target file already exists:

- **Doesn't exist** → create the folder if needed, write, continue.
- **Already exists** → DO NOT overwrite it directly. Show the user a summary of the current
  content and ask what to do: overwrite (this run's result replaces it), save as a comparison
  file, or cancel. STOP until the user answers.

## After Completion

**This command does NOT trigger `caf-orchestrator` or any automated pipeline.**
No downstream agent is spawned, no ticket status is changed, no comment/PR is posted to the
tracker. The only output is a local file in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` for a human to read.

If the user agrees with this preview and wants to proceed to the automated pipeline, they
still have to do it themselves as usual (set the ticket status to "Ready for AI" in the tracker, or whatever trigger this project uses) — remind them of this at the end of the
run, don't let the user think the pipeline has already started.

# Plan (Spec-First)

**This command writes nothing itself and touches no application code.** The only writes are the
planner's, inside `.caf/tasks/`. It does not approve the spec and it does not start
implementation.

Purpose: the chat path to the Planner's spec workflow (Specify, Clarify, Plan, Tasks) for one
piece of work, with or without a ticket. The rules of that workflow — the format of
`requirements.md`, when to ask a human, how tasks are tied to acceptance criteria — are in the
`## Output` of `caf-planner` (`.claude/agents/caf-planner.md`) and are deliberately not repeated here. This
command decides only where the artifacts go and what the planner is given.

## 1. Input

`$ARGUMENTS` is ONE of:

- **A ticket ID** — a single tracker key with no spaces (e.g. `GAN-44`). Fetch the ticket
  (title, description, acceptance criteria): if an MCP tracker (Linear/Jira/GitHub Issues) is
  connected, use it. Otherwise ask the user to paste the ticket details and **STOP** until
  answered — don't invent requirements that weren't stated.
- **Free text** — anything else. The text is the request itself, taken as-is.

`$ARGUMENTS` is empty → ask the user what to plan, **STOP** until answered. A single word that
could be either a ticket ID or a request → ask which one it is, don't guess.

## 2. Artifact Folder

Every artifact of this work goes in `.caf/tasks/<ID-or-slug>/`:

- **Ticket ID** → the ID exactly as given (e.g. `.caf/tasks/GAN-44/`).
- **Free text** → a short kebab-case slug of the text: lowercase, words joined by `-`, at most
  five words, the ones that name the work (e.g. `add CSV export to the orders page` →
  `add-csv-export-orders-page`). Tell the user the slug: it is the name this work keeps for
  every later artifact.

Don't create the folder yourself — the planner does, in step 4. If the folder already exists,
don't pick another name silently: step 3 decides. For free text only: if the existing
`requirements.md` is plainly about a different request, ask the user whether to continue that
one or to use another slug, **STOP** until answered.

## 3. Existing Spec

Read `.caf/tasks/<ID-or-slug>/requirements.md` if it exists, and look at its `Status:` line.

- **No file** → a new spec. Go to step 4.
- **`Status: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`** → the planner stopped on questions only a human can answer.
  - Every such question has its answer filled in (in the file, or given by the user in chat
    now) → continue: go to step 4 and resume from the existing file. An answer given in chat is
    passed to the planner verbatim; the planner records it, you don't answer for the user.
  - Any is still unanswered → show those questions to the user, **STOP** until answered.
- **`Status: APPROVED`** → the spec is a contract. This run does not change its goal, scope or
  acceptance criteria — not even when the argument or the user asks for it. Go to step 4 for the
  task breakdown only; a change the spec seems to need is written as a proposal in
  `verify-report.md` in the same folder, for a human to decide.
- **Any other status, or no `Status:` line** → tell the user what the file says and continue
  from it in step 4 (the planner decides what is still missing).

## 4. Spawn `caf-planner` (`.claude/agents/caf-planner.md`)

Spawn it with the Task tool. The spawn prompt MUST include:

- The input from step 1: the ticket details, or the free text verbatim — and which of the two
  it is.
- The artifact folder from step 2, with the instruction to use `<ID-or-slug>` as its
  `{TICKET-ID}` for every artifact.
- What step 3 found: a new spec; or an existing spec to resume, with the answers the user gave
  in chat; or an approved spec — goal, scope and acceptance criteria stay as they are, proposals
  go to `verify-report.md`.
- The instruction to follow the spec workflow in the `## Output` of its own definition, every
  step in order, and to stop where that workflow says to stop.
- That this is a chat run: a human reads the result and can answer.

Don't add rules of your own to the prompt and don't summarize the planner's: a rule that is
written twice will be changed in only one place.

Wait for the spawn to finish before proceeding to step 5.

## 5. Stop

Read what the planner left in `.caf/tasks/<ID-or-slug>/`, starting with the `Status:` line of
`requirements.md`:

- **`Status: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION` or `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN`** → the planner stopped on something
  only a human can settle. Show the user the questions, or the reason the planner recorded, and
  tell them to answer or decide and then run this command again with the same argument. Then
  **STOP**. Do not run any other agent: a `tasks.md` written next to such a status is not ready
  to be worked from.
- **`tasks.md` is written** (any other status) → show the user a brief summary: the folder, the
  status of `requirements.md`, how many acceptance criteria and tasks, and the assumptions or
  open questions the planner recorded. When the status is `Status: APPROVED`, say that the spec is
  approved and ready to be implemented. Then **STOP**.
- **Neither** → report exactly what is in the folder and what is missing. Don't write the
  missing file yourself.

Do not start implementation, do not spawn another agent, and do not approve the spec: setting
`Status: APPROVED` is the human's decision, made after reading `requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- This command NEVER writes or edits application code, NEVER runs `git`, NEVER changes ticket
  status in the tracker and NEVER posts to the tracker or to a PR.
- One source for the planning rules: `caf-planner` (`.claude/agents/caf-planner.md`). If that file doesn't
  exist, **STOP** and tell the user to generate it with `caf-init scaffold agents` — don't plan
  from memory.
- An approved `requirements.md` is never edited by this command or by the planner it spawns.
- It ends at `tasks.md`. Approving the spec and running the implementation are separate,
  deliberate steps taken by the user.

# Review (Initial, Pre-existing PR)

**THIS COMMAND CREATES A NEW PR REVIEW ON GITHUB.** Its side effect is real and public — a PR
Review (APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES/COMMENT) appears on someone else's PR timeline. This isn't a
read-only command — only run it when you actually intend to review this PR right now.

Purpose: the interactive path for the Reviewer Agent's INITIAL mode — reviewing from scratch a
PR that has never been reviewed by anyone (human or bot), distinct from `/caf-fix-review`
(reactive mode, responding to a human reviewer's comment on an ALREADY-reviewed PR) and distinct
from the `caf-reviewer` (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) pre-PR gate (triggered automatically in the
pipeline, not manually post-PR).

## 0. Permission Check (REQUIRED, before any step below)

`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission --jq .permission`

`{username}` is the user running this command — obtained from `gh api user --jq .login`.
Save this `{username}` result, it's reused in step 0.7 to check for an existing review.

Result is NOT one of `write`, `maintain`, `admin` → **STOP, do not process
anything further.** NO error message to the user, NO review/comment to GitHub —
the command stops silently, only log internally if needed (e.g. one log line if there's a
mechanism for it) for an audit trail if necessary. This is not a bug, it's by design: the
CAF-PRREVIEW-01 whitelist trigger is deliberately designed to not leak to outside parties
that this command was ever invoked by an unauthorized user.

(This threshold refers to a single source: `.ai/tasks/CAF-PRREVIEW-01/plan.md` §5 — if the
threshold changes, update it there first, then here, in `/caf-fix-review`, AND on the
caf-orchestrator webhook side Checkpoint B. DO NOT update just one side.)

## 0.5 Resolve PR Number & TICKET-ID

The `$ARGUMENTS` argument is a **PR number** (e.g. `81`), **NOT a TICKET-ID** — consistent
with `/caf-fix-review`, don't mix them up.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is provided** → use it directly as the PR number, proceed to TICKET-ID
resolution below.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is empty** → auto-detect from the active branch (exact same pattern as
`/caf-fix-review` — reuse its logic, don't rewrite it differently):

```
git branch --show-current
```

- Matches pattern `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` → find its PR:
  ```
  gh pr list --head ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} --json number,url
  ```
  - Exactly one PR found → use its number, proceed.
  - No PR found for that branch → ask the user for the PR number directly, **STOP** until
    answered. Don't guess.
- Active branch does NOT match the `ai-agent/*` pattern → ask the user for the PR number
  directly, **STOP** until answered.

**TICKET-ID resolution** (needed for the `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` path — see step 1),
is DERIVED from the PR already resolved above, **not detected separately again**:

```
gh pr view {number} --json headRefName,baseRefName,url
```

Parse the `ai-agent/(.+)` pattern from the resulting `headRefName` — this regex is THE SAME
as the one used by `caf-orchestrator` (`AI_AGENT_BRANCH_PATTERN` in `run-pr-review.use-case.ts`),
keep them in sync if either side changes.

- Matches → that's the TICKET-ID.
- The PR isn't from that branch pattern (a manual PR, not the result of `/caf-run-pipeline` or
  caf-orchestrator) → ask the user for the TICKET-ID manually, **STOP** until answered. Don't make
  up a TICKET-ID from a branch name with an unclear pattern.

Save the resolved `{owner}`, `{repo}` (from `gh repo view --json owner,name`),
`{number}`, `{headRefName}`, `{baseRefName}`, and `{TICKET-ID}` — used in all
subsequent steps.

## 0.7 Check for an Existing Review (idempotency)

This command can be invoked manually even if the PR has already been reviewed before (e.g. via
the `caf-orchestrator` webhook, or a previous `/caf-review` run) — check first so reviews
don't pile up without the user's knowledge.

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews
```

Filter the result: look for an entry with `user.login == {username}` (the result resolved in
step 0 — the same user/token runs this command every time it's invoked).

- **Found a previous review from `{username}`** → show the user: timestamp
  (`submitted_at`), `state` (APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED/COMMENTED), and the old review's
  `html_url`. Ask explicitly: proceed with a new review (piling up on the PR timeline), or
  cancel? Input other than yes/no → ask again, don't guess. User chooses cancel → **STOP**, no
  side effects after this.
- **Not found** (not yet reviewed by `{username}`) → proceed silently to step 1.

Reviews from OTHER actors (other human reviewers, other bots) don't count toward this
idempotency check — not relevant to deciding "has this command already run on this PR or not".

## 1. Read Task Artifacts (optional, best-effort)

Find the artifact folder of the work this PR belongs to — `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`. The
`{TICKET-ID}` is the one step 0.5 already resolved, in that order: the argument gives the PR,
the PR gives its head branch, the branch gives the ticket ID (or the user gave the ticket ID
when asked). Don't search for a folder under any other name.

The reviewer checks the change against these files, when they are there:

- `requirements.md` (the spec)
- `tasks.md`
- `design.md`
- `verify-report.md`

Check each file with `test -f` (or read directly and catch not-found) before
assuming it exists. Then keep ONE of these two results for steps 3, 4 and 5:

- **Folder found, with `requirements.md`** → a review against the spec. Note which of the
  other files are there and which are missing.
- **Folder not found, or it has no `requirements.md`** → a **code-only review**: there is no
  spec to check the change against. **DO NOT fail or STOP** — a PR reviewed by this command
  isn't necessarily from the CAF pipeline (could be a manual PR), so the review of the code
  still runs. But it is no longer silent: steps 4 and 5 say that no spec was checked.

## 2. Fetch the PR Diff

```
gh pr diff {number}
```

Save the result (plus `{headRefName}`, `{baseRefName}` from the 0.5 resolution) as the main
context carried into the step 3 spawn — this is what's being reviewed, not the task artifact
from step 1 (that artifact is just additional context).

## 3. Spawn `caf-reviewer` (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) — INITIAL mode

The spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not call `gh api` at all against GitHub, do not change ticket status in the tracker, do not fix any code — write `review-notes.md` only, in the usual format (Verdict, Security Audit, Qualitative Review, etc). Communicating back to GitHub (posting the PR Review) is the job of this command's main thread, done after you finish.

In addition to the prohibition above, the prompt MUST include:
- **Explicit mode: INITIAL** — a FULL review of this PR's diff from scratch, using the same
  criteria & golden examples as the usual pre-PR review (security audit checklist, qualitative
  review, verdict APPROVE/CHANGES REQUESTED/DEFER — see `.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md` for the
  full format). This is NOT the `/caf-fix-review` fix-comment mode — there's no human
  reviewer comment being responded to.
- `commentContext = []` (empty array, as-is — no comments to carry over, unlike
  `/caf-fix-review` which carries thread history).
- The TICKET-ID (resolved in 0.5 — don't re-detect it here).
- The PR diff from step 2.
- The result of step 1, as ONE of these two — never both, never neither:
  - The artifact folder `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` and which of its files exist, with the
    instruction to check the change against the spec the way the `## Output` of
    `.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md` describes. The reviewer reads the files itself; don't paste
    or summarize them, and don't pretend a missing file exists.
  - Or, when step 1 found no spec: the statement that this is a **code-only review** — there
    is no spec for this PR, so the reviewer does the security audit and the qualitative review
    of the diff, makes no claim about scope or acceptance criteria, and says in
    `Verdict Rationale` that no spec was checked.
- Instructions to write `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md` — format EXACTLY as defined
  in `.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md` (Ticket, Agent, Verdict, Security Audit, Qualitative Review,
  Verdict Rationale, For Developer) — **don't invent a new structure**, reuse the existing one.

Wait for the spawn to finish before proceeding to step 4.

## 4. Post GitHub PR Review

Read `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md` from step 3. Take the `Verdict` from it,
map it to a GitHub PR Review `event` (this mapping is this command's own decision, NOT
defined in `caf-reviewer.md`):

| Verdict (review-notes.md) | GitHub `event` |
|---|---|
| APPROVE | `APPROVE` |
| CHANGES REQUESTED | `REQUEST_CHANGES` |
| DEFER | `COMMENT` |

A verdict OTHER than these three (e.g. `NEEDS_HUMAN` — that value is defined in
`caf-reviewer.md` for the pipeline's automatic retry cycle, NOT for this single-run manual
command) or capitalization/spelling that doesn't match exactly → **STOP**, show the raw
`Verdict` to the user, ask which GitHub event to use manually. Don't guess or default
silently to `COMMENT`.

`body` = a summary of `review-notes.md` (Verdict Rationale + a concise list of
Blockers/Non-blockers — not the entire raw file pasted in, but complete enough that a human
reviewer doesn't have to open the file to get the gist).

When step 1 ended in a code-only review, the `body` MUST say so in its own sentence, before
the summary: the code was reviewed, and no spec was found for this PR, so scope and acceptance
criteria were not checked. An approval that leaves this out reads as an approval of the spec
too. The verdict and the `event` mapping above don't change because of it.

`comments[]` (optional) — if `review-notes.md` has findings with a specific `path`+`line`
that can be mapped to the PR diff (e.g. from a Security Audit section naming a specific file),
include them as per-file inline comments:

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews -X POST \
  -f event="{APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT}" \
  -f body="{summary}" \
  -f 'comments[][path]=...' -f 'comments[][line]=...' -f 'comments[][body]=...'
```

(or a JSON payload via `--input -` if there's more than one `comments[]` entry — pick
whichever approach is valid for multiple comments, don't assume there's only one.)

Findings without a clear `path`+`line` (general, qualitative concerns) → go into `body`
only, don't force them into an inline comment.

**If the `gh api` call above fails with `422 Unprocessable Entity`** — check the
`errors[]` field in the response:

- Contains `"Can not approve your own pull request"` (event `APPROVE`) OR
  `"Can not request changes on your own pull request"` (event `REQUEST_CHANGES`) — confirmed
  empirically (PR #83/GAN-114, 2026-08-22): the GitHub API rejects both of these events when the
  user running the command (the `gh` token) is the same as the PR author, with a different
  message per event, not one generic message. `COMMENT` is NOT subject to this restriction
  (confirmed to succeed when posting on your own PR). → **STOP, don't retry automatically with
  a different event.** Show the user: this PR is authored by the same user running the
  command — the GitHub API rejected `{original event}` for their own PR. Offer two explicit
  options, let the user choose (don't default to either):
  1. **Post as `COMMENT`** — `body` MUST start with an explicit statement of the actual
     verdict on the first line, e.g.: `"⚠ Actual verdict: {APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES} — posted as
     COMMENT because the GitHub API rejected self-{approve|request-changes}."`, followed by the
     usual summary. **Don't silently downgrade** — this statement must actually appear in the
     body that gets posted, not just be noted in a local log.
  2. **Cancel** — no PR Review gets posted. Suggest the user ask another reviewer/token to run
     the command.
- `errors[]` does NOT match either pattern above (some other cause — e.g. PR already
  closed/merged, malformed `comments[]`) → **STOP as usual**, show the raw error message to the
  user. Don't assume this is a self-review case.

## 5. Summary to the User

Show in chat: the final Verdict, the GitHub event used, a link to the newly created PR Review
(from the step 4 `gh api` response), and the location of `review-notes.md` for full details.

Also say which review this was: against the spec in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` (name the
artifact files that were missing, if any), or a code-only review because step 1 found no spec.

## Constraints

- This command NEVER runs `git push`, NEVER checks out/commits code, NEVER changes ticket
  status in the tracker — the only writes are `review-notes.md` (subagent) and the new
  PR Review on GitHub (main thread, step 4).
- The idempotency check (step 0.7) ONLY detects a previous `/caf-review` run (whether from
  this command itself, from the same `{username}`). **CAF-ORCH-PRREVIEW-03 (caf-orchestrator,
  2026-09-04)**: the webhook's mode `initial` now runs the same real INITIAL (Verdict-producing)
  contract as this command and posts via `pulls/{number}/reviews` too (`RunPrReviewUseCase` →
  `IVcsClient.createPullRequestReview`) — the artifact-contract mismatch that used to make
  `GET pulls/{number}/reviews` blind to the webhook's review is gone. What's **STILL NOT
  detected**: actor-login mismatch — this step filters by `user.login == {username}` (the human
  running this command), but the webhook posts under the pipeline's own bot/token login, so a
  prior webhook-triggered review still won't match here even though it now exists as the same
  kind of PR Review object. Genuine remaining gap, tracked separately (not in
  CAF-ORCH-PRREVIEW-03's scope, which explicitly excluded it) — see
  `.ai/tasks/CAF-PRREVIEW-01/open-items.md` (caf-initiator).
- Inline `comments[]` (step 4) depends on `review-notes.md` naming an explicit
  `path`+`line` for its findings — if the reviewer only gives a general concern without a
  clear location, the review still gets posted but without an inline comment (it all goes into
  the `body` summary).
- This Checkpoint A (caf-initiator) isn't yet wired to an automatic webhook — this command is
  always triggered manually by the user. Automatic triggering for a new PR (e.g. fired on the
  `opened` event) is caf-orchestrator's scope, outside this command.
- This command CANNOT produce a PR Review with event `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`
  if the user running the command is the author of the PR being reviewed — this is a
  restriction from the GitHub API itself (confirmed empirically, PR #83/GAN-114, 2026-08-22:
  both are rejected with `422` and a different message per event), not a bug in this command.
  The available fallback (see step 4): post as `COMMENT` with the actual verdict stated
  explicitly on the first line of the `body`, or cancel entirely — the command never silently
  downgrades the event without user confirmation.

# Run Pipeline (Manual, No Orchestrator)

**This command WRITES CODE and CREATES A BRANCH.** It's the only command generated by
caf-initiator that does both — treat it more carefully than the others.

Purpose: a manual alternative for projects that haven't set up (or don't want) `caf-orchestrator`
(webhook + VPS). The flow mirrors the automated pipeline, including **auto-commit, auto-push, and
auto `gh pr create`** after Reviewer APPROVE — see section 7. No ticket status is changed in the
tracker (that stays manual); only git + PR are automated.

**If it stops at NEEDS_HUMAN** (implementation, Validator gate, or Reviewer gate): there is NO commit,
push, or PR at all — the working tree is left as-is on branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` for a human.
See "Controlled Stop" below.

Boundary worth knowing: the `allowed-tools` allowlist above binds this command (MAIN THREAD),
**not the spawned subagents** — subagents run with the tools from their own agent definition.
That's why every spawn prompt below MUST explicitly include the push/PR prohibition ("that's the
main thread's job in section 7, not yours") — commit/push/PR may happen only once, in section 7,
performed by the main thread after all gates pass.

## Ticket

Ticket ID: `$ARGUMENTS`

Required. If empty, ask the user which ticket is meant and STOP until answered — don't guess.

Fetch ticket details (title, description, acceptance criteria): if a tracker MCP is connected
(Linear/Jira/GitHub Issues), use it. Otherwise, ask the user to paste the ticket details manually
before continuing — don't invent requirements that weren't stated.

## 0. Guard — required, before spawning anything

Run these four checks **sequentially and to completion** before the Task tool is used at all.
Don't spawn any agent "while waiting for the user's answer".

### 0.1 Working directory must be clean

`git status --porcelain`. If there's output (uncommitted changes) → **STOP**, show the list, ask
the user to commit/stash first. Don't check out a new branch with changes that could get carried
along or lost.

### 0.2 Does branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` already exist?

Check **both local AND remote** — both, not just one:

```
git branch --list ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
git ls-remote --heads origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

Checking remote isn't a formality: `caf-orchestrator` runs on a VPS, so if it has already/is
currently handling this ticket, its branch shows up on the **remote** and may not exist in the
user's working copy at all. A local-only check would pass exactly in the most dangerous case.

If this repo has no `origin` remote at all (`git ls-remote` fails with "'origin' does not appear
to be a git repository"), that's **not a guard failure** — a purely local repo simply can't be
claimed by the orchestrator. Note "remote: none", proceed with the local check result only. Don't
STOP because of this, and don't treat the remote check as passed either.

- **Not present in either** → proceed to 0.3.
- **Present in either/both** → **STOP**. This is a strong signal this ticket is already/currently
  being handled by the orchestrator or a previous `/caf-run-pipeline` run. Show the user:
  - `git log --oneline` for that branch (whatever commits already exist there),
  - the contents of `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md` if it exists,
  - whether it was local, remote, or both.

  Then ask for explicit confirmation: **continue on that branch**, or **abort**. DO NOT assume
  it's safe to continue, and DO NOT create a new branch that overwrites it. If the user chooses
  to continue, `git checkout ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` (not `-b`).

  **Limitation you must disclose to the user at this point:** an orchestrator run that just
  started and hasn't pushed its branch yet is NOT detected by this check. If the user knows an
  automated pipeline is currently running for this ticket, abort — regardless of the check
  results above.

### 0.3 Already completed before?

Check `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md`.

If that file exists and its status is **not** `NEEDS_HUMAN` → **STOP**. This ticket has likely
already been completed. Show its summary, ask the user: **restart from scratch (override)** or
**abort**. Don't silently overwrite completed work.

Deliberately phrased as "not NEEDS_HUMAN" rather than "equals SUCCESS": the success label in
`verify-report.md` isn't consistent across sources (CAF.md calls it `SUCCESS`, the handoff
template calls it `PASS`, and agents in the wild sometimes write `DONE`). The only consistent
marker is `NEEDS_HUMAN` for "not yet done". Matching the exact string `SUCCESS` would make this
guard silently never fire — exactly the failure it's meant to prevent.

If the status is `NEEDS_HUMAN`, don't STOP: this ticket was genuinely left unfinished. Tell the
user this run continues previously interrupted work, then proceed.

### 0.4 Create the branch

Only after 0.1-0.3 pass: `git checkout -b ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` from the currently active branch.
If the user already chose "continue" in 0.2, the branch is already checked out — skip this step.

## 1. Planner (required)

Spawn Planner. Its source of truth is `.claude/agents/caf-planner.md` — read that file and follow
it. Input: ticket details from the Ticket section above.

Required output: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md` and `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/tasks.md`.

If Planner reports the ticket is too ambiguous to break down, **STOP the entire pipeline** —
report to the user and ask for ticket clarification. Don't proceed to implementation with a plan
Planner itself says it isn't confident about.

## 2. Architect (conditional)

This stage is **conditional** — don't always spawn it.

Spawn Architect (`.claude/agents/caf-architect.md`) ONLY if either is true:

- `tasks.md` from Planner explicitly states it needs an architecture/design decision, OR
- the task touches more than one app/service, OR involves a new schema/migration.

If the ticket is simple and single-app, **skip** — go on to stage 3. Producing `design.md`
for a task that doesn't need it just adds run cost and a document nobody reads.

Output: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/design.md`. If skipped, note in the final summary that this
stage was skipped along with the reason — don't let it silently disappear from the report.

## Spec Status Check (before any implementation agent)

Before stage 3 spawns an implementation agent, read `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md` and
look at its `Status:` line and at its questions.

- `Status: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION`, or any question tagged `BLOCKING` that has no `Answer:` →
  **STOP the entire pipeline** and go straight to the Final Summary with `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN`.
  Show the user those questions, word for word, so they can answer them in `requirements.md`.
  Spawn no implementation agent: code written on an unanswered question is the guess the spec was
  meant to prevent.
- `Status: DRAFT` or `Status: APPROVED` → go on. Only an unanswered question stops the run,
  not the draft state of the spec.

This command NEVER writes or edits `requirements.md` or `tasks.md`, whatever the status: the
planner writes them and a human decides them.

**A proposed change to the spec is shown, never applied.** Whenever a stage proposes one — under
`## Proposed Spec Changes` in `verify-report.md`, in a line of the gate report that starts with
`Proposed Spec Changes:`, or in what the Reviewer copied into `### For Developer` of
`review-notes.md` — copy it as written into the Final Summary for a human to decide. Do not accept
it, do not reject it, and do not apply it: not to `requirements.md`, not to `tasks.md`, not to
the code.

## 3. Implementation

Implementation agents available in this project:

- `caf-frontend` (`.claude/agents/caf-frontend.md`)
- `caf-backend` (`.claude/agents/caf-backend.md`)

**How to choose which agent to spawn** (this decision must NOT be guessed):

1. Read the app/module column of each task in `tasks.md`.
2. Match it against each agent's scope above — read `## Scope` in the agent's file, don't
   guess from its name.
3. A task whose app/module matches one agent's scope → that agent handles it.
4. If a task doesn't match any agent's scope, OR matches more than one, **ask the user**
   which agent should handle it and STOP until answered.
   Misrouting means an agent writes code outside its scope — a silent failure only caught at
   review time.
5. An agent with no tasks at all: DO NOT spawn it. Not a failure — there's simply no work for
   it on this ticket.

If multiple agents have tasks, run them **sequentially, not in parallel** — both write to the
same working tree. Order follows the task dependencies in `tasks.md`.

Input for each agent: `requirements.md`, `tasks.md`, and `design.md` if stage 2 ran.

Every spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours. Write only the code and
> `verify-report.md`, on the branch that's already active.

**Internal PIV is that agent's own concern.** Implementation agents already have their own Retry
Logic (implement → verify → fix, max 3x) in their definition. You are **NOT** allowed to respawn
an implementation agent just because its verify failed — that would effectively double the retry
budget. The only respawn path is the gate retries in stages 5 and 6.

If an agent finishes with `verify-report.md` `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN`:
**STOP the entire pipeline here.** Don't proceed to Documentation/Validator/Reviewer with code whose
verify hasn't passed — every subsequent stage would produce a report about code already known to
be broken, and that's wasted cost.

## 4. Documentation (non-blocking)

This project has no Documentation Agent (`.claude/agents/caf-documentation.md` was not
generated) — skip this stage, note "not available" in the final summary. This is not a
pipeline failure.

## 5. Validator (gate)

The Validator (`.claude/agents/caf-validator.md`) spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**Gate — `validatorRetryCount`, `MAX_VALIDATOR_RETRIES = 1`.**

Set `validatorRetryCount = 0` at the start of this run. This counter is **fresh every time
`/caf-run-pipeline` runs** and **independent** of other gate counters — budget exhausted on
one gate does NOT reduce another gate's budget. Don't treat it as a shared budget.

Flow:

1. Spawn Validator (`.claude/agents/caf-validator.md`), wait for its result.
2. Result OK → proceed to the next stage.
3. Result `FAIL`:
   - If `validatorRetryCount >= MAX_VALIDATOR_RETRIES` → **STOP here**, report NEEDS_HUMAN (see
     "Controlled Stop" below).
   - Otherwise → increment `validatorRetryCount` by 1 from its previous value, then **respawn the
     relevant implementation agent** with `validate-report.md` as input, asking it to fix only the
     findings (not redo the implementation from scratch). Once the fix is done, run this gate
     **once more**, back to step 1.
4. Budget exhausted (`validatorRetryCount >= MAX_VALIDATOR_RETRIES`) and the gate still fails → STOP,
   NEEDS_HUMAN.

Retry means **fix, then re-check** — not running the gate twice over the exact same code.
Re-running the gate with nothing changed just burns cost for a result that's already certain to
be the same.

`UNVERIFIED` rows do NOT fail the gate — that's intentional, not an overlooked gap. If
`validate-report.md` closes with `Status: PASS`, treat it as "Result OK" and proceed to the next
stage, and copy its `Unverified:` line into the Final Summary so a human sees which criteria
were not confirmed. Only `Status: FAIL` triggers the retry gate.

`Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` means the validation could not be done at all (nothing to fix in the code):
**STOP here** and report NEEDS_HUMAN without using the retry budget.

Artifact: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/validate-report.md`.

## 6. Reviewer (gate)

The Reviewer (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**Gate — `reviewerRetryCount`, `MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES = 1`.**

Set `reviewerRetryCount = 0` at the start of this run. This counter is **fresh every time
`/caf-run-pipeline` runs** and **independent** of other gate counters — budget exhausted on
one gate does NOT reduce another gate's budget. Don't treat it as a shared budget.

Flow:

1. Spawn Reviewer (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`), wait for its result.
2. Result OK → proceed to the next stage.
3. Result `REQUEST_CHANGES / NEEDS_HUMAN`:
   - If `reviewerRetryCount >= MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES` → **STOP here**, report NEEDS_HUMAN (see
     "Controlled Stop" below).
   - Otherwise → increment `reviewerRetryCount` by 1 from its previous value, then **respawn the
     relevant implementation agent** with `review-notes.md` (BLOCKING findings only) as input, asking it to fix only the
     findings (not redo the implementation from scratch). Once the fix is done, run this gate
     **once more**, back to step 1.
4. Budget exhausted (`reviewerRetryCount >= MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES`) and the gate still fails → STOP,
   NEEDS_HUMAN.

Retry means **fix, then re-check** — not running the gate twice over the exact same code.
Re-running the gate with nothing changed just burns cost for a result that's already certain to
be the same.

Artifact: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md`.

To be explicit: `reviewerRetryCount` is **not affected** by what happens in the Validator stage. A
ticket whose Validator passed after a retry still enters this stage with a full budget of 1.

## 7. Commit, Push, PR (SUCCESS)

**This stage runs ONLY if Reviewer APPROVEs.** If the pipeline stopped at any stage before this
(implementation NEEDS_HUMAN, Validator/Reviewer gate exhausted), **skip this entire section** and go
straight to "Controlled Stop" below — don't commit anything.

Run these seven steps **in order**. Any step with a STOP condition must halt there, not proceed
to the next step — a commit with the wrong scope or a push that collides with the remote branch
can't easily be undone once it happens.

### 7.1 Scope whitelist

Paths allowed into the commit (ONLY these, not the entire working tree):

- `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` (artifact)
- `caf-frontend`: `apps/web/`
- `caf-backend`: `apps/api/`

`git status --porcelain` → match **every** changed path against the whitelist above.

A path changed BUT not in any whitelist → **STOP, DO NOT commit anything**. Show the suspicious
paths to the user, explain this is likely a file outside the assigned agent's scope (a bug or
scope creep in a subagent). Ask the user to decide manually — commit anyway after verifying, or
investigate first. In the Final Summary, record the status as "SUCCESS but commit aborted —
scope drift detected", not a plain SUCCESS status.

### 7.2 Commit

`git add --` followed by the explicit list of paths from 7.1 that actually changed (**not**
`git add -A`), then:

```
git commit -m "AI agent pipeline: {TICKET-ID}"
```

Without `--allow-empty`. If the commit fails because there's nothing to commit ("nothing to
commit") — that's an odd signal (implementation reported done but there's no diff at all) →
**STOP**, report to the user, don't proceed to push/PR.

### 7.3 Guard — fetch before push

```
git fetch origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

If fetch fails because the branch doesn't exist on the remote at all, that's not a guard
failure — proceed treating it as "remote doesn't exist yet" (next step).

- **Remote doesn't exist** → safe, proceed to 7.4.
- **Remote exists**, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} HEAD`
  succeeds (exit 0) → the remote SHA is an ancestor of local HEAD, safe, proceed to 7.4.
- **Remote exists**, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails (exit != 0) → the remote SHA is
  NOT an ancestor of local HEAD. **STOP before pushing.** This signals the remote branch has been
  changed by another party (the orchestrator, or another `/caf-run-pipeline` run) since guard
  0.2 ran at the start of this command. Show the user: the remote SHA, `git log --oneline` of
  that remote branch, and the local commit just created in 7.2 (still in the working tree, not
  yet pushed). **DO NOT force-push, DO NOT auto merge/rebase** — that's a human decision.

**Limitation to disclose to the user at this point**: this is best-effort, not an absolute
guarantee — a race condition between this fetch-check and the push in 7.4 is still possible
(small window, but real) if another party pushes exactly between the two steps. There's no
distributed lock available from this command's side to close that gap entirely — same pattern of
limitation as guard 0.2.

### 7.4 Push

```
git push --set-upstream origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

### 7.5 Detect base branch

```
gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name
```

Save the result as `{BASE-BRANCH}`. **Don't hardcode `main`** — the target repo might use
`master`, `develop`, or another name.

### 7.6 Check for an existing PR (idempotency)

```
gh pr list --head ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} --state open --json url,number
```

- **Result found** → a PR for this branch already exists (e.g. opened manually by the user after

## Controlled Stop (NEEDS_HUMAN)

If any gate exhausts its budget, or implementation ends in NEEDS_HUMAN: that's a **controlled
stop, not an error**. Don't throw an exception, don't make the command look like it "crashed",
don't try an alternative path not instructed here.

What to do: stop at that stage, go straight to the Final Summary with status NEEDS_HUMAN and
state which stage stopped it plus what findings remain unresolved. Code already written stays on
the branch — don't revert it, don't delete it. A human decides whether to continue or discard it.

**To be explicit: the NEEDS_HUMAN path never reaches section 7.** There is no commit, push, or PR
at all on this path — the working tree is left exactly as the last stage that stopped the
pipeline left it. This isn't new behavior (it's already implied by the stop/`return` structure
in each gate), written explicitly here to remove ambiguity.

Before writing the final summary, confirm with Bash/Read — not from memory of the flow.

**If the run ended NEEDS_HUMAN:**

- [ ] The artifact for every stage that ran actually exists in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`
- [ ] **No push happened** — `git status -sb`: the first line must not mention an upstream

      `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` for this check: if the branch has genuinely never been
      pushed, that ref doesn't exist and the command errors instead of giving an answer.
- [ ] If it turns out something was pushed by a subagent, **report it prominently to the user**
      in the final summary — that's a violation of this command's contract, not a minor detail.

**If the run ended SUCCESS (section 7 ran):**

- [ ] The currently active branch really is `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`
- [ ] A push actually happened — `git status -sb` mentions the upstream
      `origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`
- [ ] The PR exists — either newly created in 7.7 OR an existing one detected in 7.6, its URL is
      correct and reachable

      file outside scope got committed along with it
- [ ] If a file outside the whitelist did slip into the commit, **report it prominently to the
      user** in the final summary — that's a violation of this command's scope contract.

```
| Stage          | Status                          | Artifact |
| Planner        | SUCCESS                         | requirements.md, tasks.md |
| Architect      | SUCCESS / SKIP (reason)         | design.md |

| Validator      | PASS (retry: n/1) / NEEDS_HUMAN / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | validate-report.md |
| Reviewer       | APPROVE (retry: n/1) / NEEDS_HUMAN / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | review-notes.md |
| Commit/Push/PR | SUCCESS (new/existing PR) / ABORTED (scope drift) / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | commit + PR URL |
```

ran and found a problem, when it didn't. Its artifact doesn't exist either, so write `-` in the
